notes: The catalogue card for arduino-yun lists no digital pin ports (only VIN, 3V3, GND, USB_MICRO, USB_A, ETHERNET, MICROSD). I used port '9' for digital pin 9 as the tutorial and image show. This port name is not on the card, so it may need adding to the catalogue.

Breadboard strips: the image shows the 5-hole strips running horizontally, so I treated each horizontal row as one column-bank strip. Strip 10t takes the red wire (a) and R1 leg 1 (b). Strip 14t takes R1 leg 2 (b) and the LED anode (e). Strip 13t takes the black wire (a) and the LED cathode (e). The exact column numbers are my choice, but the strip topology follows the image.
Circuit follows the schematic: D9 -> 220Ω R1 -> LED anode, LED cathode -> GND. The LED's bent (longer) leg is the anode, on the resistor side.
The Yún is powered over USB, which the tutorial doesn't show, so no cable was added.
